introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Further Mathematics Paper 2 (0775), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2023. Time allowed: three hours.**

Answer ALL 10 questions. For your guidance, the approximate mark allocation for parts of each question is indicated. Mathematical formulae and tables published by the Board, and noiseless non-programmable electronic calculators are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Solve completely the complex equation
$$z^{3} = -8i.$$ (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Write $-8i$ in modulus-argument form: $|-8i| = 8$ and $\arg(-8i) = -\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, so
$$z^{3} = 8\left[\cos\left(-\tfrac{\pi}{2} + 2k\pi\right) + i\sin\left(-\tfrac{\pi}{2} + 2k\pi\right)\right], \quad k \in \mathbb{Z}.$$
By De Moivre's theorem, the cube roots have modulus $8^{1/3} = 2$ and arguments
$$\theta_k = \frac{-\tfrac{\pi}{2} + 2k\pi}{3} = -\frac{\pi}{6} + \frac{2k\pi}{3}, \qquad k = 0, 1, 2.$$

- $k = 0$: $\theta = -\dfrac{\pi}{6}$, $z = 2\left(\cos\dfrac{\pi}{6} - i\sin\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = \sqrt{3} - i$.
- $k = 1$: $\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$, $z = 2\left(\cos\dfrac{\pi}{2} + i\sin\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = 2i$.
- $k = 2$: $\theta = \dfrac{7\pi}{6}$, $z = 2\left(\cos\dfrac{7\pi}{6} + i\sin\dfrac{7\pi}{6}\right) = -\sqrt{3} - i$.

$$\boxed{z = \sqrt{3} - i, \quad z = 2i, \quad z = -\sqrt{3} - i}$$
Check: $(2i)^{3} = 8i^{3} = -8i$. The three roots lie on the circle $|z| = 2$, equally spaced by $\tfrac{2\pi}{3}$.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Find the centre and scale factor of the transformation described by
$$w = 2z - 3 + 4i.$$ (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
The map $z \mapsto w = 2z - 3 + 4i$ has the form $w = kz + c$ with real $k = 2 \neq 1$, so it is an **enlargement** with scale factor $2$. Its centre is the fixed point, where $w = z$:
$$z = 2z - 3 + 4i \quad\Rightarrow\quad z = 3 - 4i.$$
Equivalently, $w - (3 - 4i) = 2\big(z - (3 - 4i)\big)$, because $2\big(z - 3 + 4i\big) + 3 - 4i = 2z - 3 + 4i$.

$$\boxed{\text{Enlargement, centre } 3 - 4i \ (\text{the point } (3, -4)),\ \text{scale factor } 2}$$
